articles.title: Council Votes on After-school Reading Program After Long Debate
articles.deck: Residents of Hickory Ridge filled the hall on Saturday to ask questions about the plan.
body: The group has raised $1,200 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

The plan calls for after-school reading program along Ridge Drive, with work expected to start in November. Esther Kim, who has lived in Hickory Ridge for 31 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Saturday mornings. Public works estimates the work will take about 31 weeks once it begins.

articles.title: Alma Kozak, 78, Piano Teacher
articles.deck: Friends remember Alma Kozak for the many years of service to Bellwood.
body: Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Bellwood. Alma Kozak died in January at home on Maple Terrace, at the age of 78.

Born in Bellwood in the years after the war, Alma Kozak spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood. Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Millrace Library branch in his or her name.

articles.title: Lower Millrace Asks Council for Speed Limit Change
articles.deck: The vote came after 10 residents spoke at Wednesday’s session.
body: Councilmember Ellis Reyes asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $18,500.

Public works estimates the work will take about 10 weeks once it starts in April. Residents of Lower Millrace said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.

Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days. The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first.
